hourly.summary: United fans are in full meltdown mode: the Reds sit in the relegation zone, ten players could miss the Anfield showdown, the January window is shuttered before it opens, and the transfer strategy is being dissected like a crime scene. Pochettino's getting pelters for his playing career and his team selection, while the recruitment brain trust is accused of paying premium prices for Championship-quality squad filler. The only thing missing is a 'Sack the Board' banner.

daily.summary: Sentiment plummeted from apprehensive resignation to outright seething rage mid-day as the 18th-place reality and drone-spying scandal hit, before settling back into a weary, gallows-humour fatalism by evening. Across all three snapshots, the dominant chords are exhaustion with the Glazer-era dysfunction, zero trust in leadership, and a grim certainty that the Pochettino appointment will merely extend the managerial merry-go-round.

weekly.summary: Fan sentiment began in existential crisis (2/10) with the club in the relegation zone and ownership rage dominant, briefly lifted by Pochettino rumors (4/10) before crashing again on Carrick's sacking (2/10). His appointment brought apprehensive hope (4-5/10) that quickly faded into disillusionment (3/10), finally settling into a dark, resigned acceptance of mediocrity (5/10) laced with gallows humor. The week traces an arc from acute despair through false dawns to cynical resignation, with structural anger at the Glazers/INEOS ownership remaining the constant undercurrent.
